simple.meaning: שְׁרֵא (shᵉrêʼ) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to free , separate ; figuratively, to unravel , commence ; by implication (of unloading beasts) to reside.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 6 times in Ezra, Daniel, beginning at Ezra 5:2. The surrounding contexts include family line, kingship, prophetic witness.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שְׁרֵא (H8271) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: שְׁרֵא (shᵉrêʼ) / H8271 is traced through Ezra 5:2, Daniel 2:22, Daniel 3:25, Daniel 5:6 with source-language evidence and verse context.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Then Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and Jeshua the son of Jozadak rose up and began to build God’s house which is at Jerusalem; and with them were the prophets of God, helping them.

timeline.evidenceText: Then Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and Jeshua the son of Jozadak rose up and began to build God’s house which is at Jerusalem; and with them were the prophets of God, helping them.
He reveals the deep and secret things.
He answered, “Look, I see four men loose, walking in the middle of the fire, and they are unharmed. The appearance of the fourth is like a son of the gods.”
Then the king’s face was changed in him, and his thoughts troubled him; and the joints of his thighs were loosened, and his knees struck one against another.

because an excellent spirit, knowledge, understanding, interpreting of dreams, showing of dark sentences, and dissolving of doubts were found in the same Daniel, whom the king named Belteshazzar. Now let Daniel be called, and he will show the interpretation.”

But I have heard of you, that you can give interpretations, and dissolve doubts. Now if you can read the writing, and make known to me its interpretation, you shall be clothed with purple, and have a chain of gold around your neck, and shall be the third ruler in the kingdom.”

definitions.full: H8271. shera [ שְׁרָא ] verb 1. loosen . 2 abide (see Biblical Hebrew I. שׁרה ); — Pe`al Infinitive לְמִשְׁרֵא Dan 5:16 ; read ׳מִשׁ also 5:12 , for ׳מְשָׁ (K § 40 n M 87* and others); — Passive participle שְׁרֵא (K § 47. Beisp. f )) 2:22 ; plural שְׁרַיִן 3:25 ; — 1 loosen: literal passive participle loosed Dan 3:25 (opposed to bound); figurative loosen knots, i.e. solve difficulties, 5:12 , 16 . 2 abide (from loosening girths, loads, at encampment; compare ᵑ7 Late Hebrew [also on passive participle]), figurative Dan 2:22 ( עִם of person). Pa`el Perfect 3masculine plural שָׁרִיו Ezra 5:2 begin (see Biblical Hebrew III. [ חָלַל ] Hiph`il 2 ), followed by infinitive Hithpa. Participle masculine plural מִשְׁתָּרַ֫יִן Dan 5:6 joints were loosened (in fear).
